item.title: ‘No basis in international law’: China rejects US tariff threat over Russian oil
item.description: China firmly rebuffs American attempts to influence nations purchasing Russian energy commodities. The US legislative proposal introduces tariffs on significant buyers of Russian oil and gas. Beijing denounces sanctions that lack a foundation in international law or UN backing. For its part, India emphasizes energy security and stays vigilant regarding US legislative actions, ready to implement measures to safeguard its trade interests.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Nicolas Cage bought Rhode Island estate for $15.7 million, sold it at a $9.5 million loss
item.description: Actor Nicolas Cage bought Rhode Island’s Gray Craig estate for $15.7 million in 2007 and listed it for $15.9 million a year later. The 27-acre property has a 24,000-square-foot stone mansion with 12 bedrooms, 10 bathrooms, ocean views, a tennis court, gym and pool. Cage eventually sold the estate for $6.2 million in 2011 to Massachusetts couple Andrew and Pamela Constantine.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Three African wild dog brothers travelled 4,126 km; the longest recorded African mammal dispersal
item.description: A trio of African wild dog brothers undertook a remarkable odyssey covering 4,126 kilometers across Zambia. This unprecedented trek marks the longest documented dispersal by a mammal in Africa. Their journey through various terrains, including natural reserves and areas impacted by humans, highlights the crucial need for habitat connectivity beyond national park borders, revealing pressing conservation issues faced by species that require large ranges.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Hiker Found After Weeklong Search: 70-year-old located alive by backpackers; Coast Guard airlifts him
item.description: After being missing for a week, 70-year-old hiker Craig Berg was miraculously found alive on Isle Royale on September 12. The search efforts proved critical, with fellow backpackers aiding in his discovery despite his injuries and hypothermia. Following his rescue, he was airlifted for urgent medical care, bringing an end to a challenging multi-agency search and rescue operation.

item.title: North Carolina acquires 342+ acres with grants; mountain moves toward Buncombe's largest park
item.description: Buncombe County is set to embark on an exciting adventure as it unveils plans for its largest public park on Deaverview Mountain. With a generous grant covering the acquisition of the expansive 342-acre property, the county recently greenlit a contract to develop a comprehensive master plan. This plan will serve as a blueprint for creating trails and visitor facilities while prioritizing passive recreation and the conservation of vital natural habitats.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Infomercial pioneer Ron Popeil’s Beverly Hills home, where he tested inventions, listed for $25 mn
item.description: Ron Popeil’s longtime Beverly Hills estate is on the market for $25 million, nearly five years after his death. Popeil and his wife bought the 2.34-acre property for $7.5 million in 2002 and raised their two daughters there. The 14,595-square-foot villa includes a commercial kitchen where Popeil tested kitchen-product prototypes, along with a screening room, gym and wine cellar.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: America's Rorshach Test: Why Sydney Sweeney makes liberals go mad
item.description: That Sydney’s body had taken on deeper meaning beyond its corporeal form and become a political battleground was evident in 2022 when she threw her mother a 60th birthday party where one guest wore a Blue Lives Matter T-shirt and others wore red caps that said “Make Sixty Great Again”. That was enough for Sweeney to be cast out of the proverbial liberal heaven by some imaginary association with the Orange One.
item.dc:creator: Nirmalya Dutta

item.title: Colorado buys 2,100-acre ranch to help save lesser prairie-chickens from decline
item.description: Colorado’s lesser prairie-chicken population has fallen from more than 80,000 birds in 1975 to only 89 breeding males in 2024. The Southern Plains Land Trust has acquired nearly 2,100 acres for just under $2 million to restore grassland habitat. The property, near an active breeding site, will be restored with Colorado Parks and Wildlife to support the species’ recovery.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Historic Steel Pier in Atlantic City hits market for $85M
item.description: For the eye-catching price of eighty-five million dollars, Atlantic City's Steel Pier, with its storied past, is now on the market. The landmark amusement park provides vast ocean development rights that could lead to exciting future ventures. Purchased by the Catanoso family for just four point two five million fourteen years ago, this beloved destination has the potential for redevelopment into vibrant entertainment or residential facilities.

item.title: Video: US forces take out floating refuelling station allegedly tied to drug trade
item.description: US forces intercepted a floating refuelling station in the Eastern Pacific on September 16. This vessel allegedly supported illicit drug trafficking operations for Ecuador's Los Choneros organization. US forces removed the crew and transferred them to Ecuadorian authorities after clearing the vessel. The refuelling station was then sunk by US forces following the operation. This action aimed to disrupt logistical networks supporting drug trafficking in the Western Hemisphere.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: In 2013, St Agnes and Gugh began rat eradication; 12 yrs later, Manx shearwater sites hit record 225
item.description: A rat eradication project on St Agnes and Gugh in the Isles of Scilly began in 2013 after invasive brown rats were found to be threatening nesting seabirds. The islands have remained rat-free since the operation, while Manx shearwater breeding numbers have increased from 22 pairs before eradication to 225 apparently occupied breeding sites recorded in 2025.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Buffalo transformed a 264-acre dump in 1976; 50 years later, 260+ bird species are recorded
item.description: In 2026, Buffalo's Tifft Nature Preserve proudly commemorates its 50th anniversary, evolving from a former landfill into a 264-acre ecological haven. The tireless restoration work has resulted in stunning wetlands, lush woodlands, and diverse wildlife ecosystems. Home to 260+ bird species, the preserve encourages exploration through its accessible trails while supporting ongoing research initiatives.
